minutes.headline: Finance Committee voted to recommend the school override article, on a roll call the captions render as four to two.
minutes.summary: With six members present, the chair moved warrant recommendations ahead of other business. The committee voted to recommend the school override article after a graph presentation on the "double dipping" question. It reversed course to recommend the parental sick leave article and the senior tax exemption article, and left Articles 4 and 5 deferred. It then workshopped the draft annual report and heard committee reports.

public_comment.topic: Asked why the school district dropped bus fees while expanding busing eligibility, called seeking town-side funds offensive, and opposed the override.
A parent of a high school student opposed funding a budget with no removable line items, doubted user fees, and suggested folding the school committee into the town budget.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee voted to recommend the school override article (Article 8); the captions garble the roll call, and it appears to have passed with one member absent.
The committee rescinded an earlier no-direct-financial-impact finding and voted to recommend the parental leave article (Article 11), with one abstention and one absence.
The committee rescinded the deferral and voted 6-0 to recommend the senior tax exemption article (Article 21), with one member absent.
Articles 4 and 5 stayed deferred, with Article 5 waiting on the snow and ice number.
The committee set April 11 to finalize the annual report and possibly vote on Articles 4 and 5; the April 25 meeting may not be needed.

why_it_matters: The override article asks voters to raise more tax than the Proposition 2.5 limit allows to supplement the schools' budget, so residents will see a ballot question and a warrant article on it.
The committee's recommendations on the parental leave and senior tax exemption articles go into the warrant that Town Meeting voters will be asked to act on.

The minutes describe some school items as covered by one-time ARPA funds, which the school committee voted to return if the override passes, so the override's effect on school spending and the tax rate depends on that choice.
